document: The executable closure of the M5 conformance campaign
note: The single source of truth for what the conformance campaign is made of. The producer reads it to record the object identity of every path at the tree it actually ran on; the verifier reads it to require those identities to still hold. Neither restates the list, because a list kept in two places is a list that will disagree.
rule: A change to anything here changes what the evidence is evidence of, so retained reports produced before the change may not be promoted after it: the campaign has to be run again. A change to anything not here — documentation, the changelog, or unrelated jobs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — leaves retained evidence valid. The dedicated `.github/workflows/m5-conformance.yml` is bound as one object, so changes to the conformance provisioning or call layer invalidate conformance evidence without binding the rest of CI.
closure_scope_note: Two things this campaign owes are not the same thing. The row-proof denominator is the 42 accepted M0-M4 rows and the 133 scenarios the accepted-scope document assigns to them; every assigned scenario must report `ok`, and every row must be proved by at least one. The execution envelope is the 30 unique `(package, target)` test binaries those 133 assignments touch; the producer derives this set from the scope document and selects exactly these targets, but each selected target is run in full — not filtered to only its assigned scenarios — so a test inside a selected target that the accepted scope never named still runs, and its exit status still gates the campaign through the failed-target check, the same as an assigned scenario's outcome does. What the envelope excludes is a workspace test target outside the 30: it used to run every workspace test target `cargo metadata` reported, which made a target the accepted scope never touched at all — including every other M5 campaign's own reconciliation test — able to fail this campaign. Two of those excluded targets read `docs/project/m5-campaign-evidence.md`, a document this campaign's own retention step rewrites with a report's provenance after the report is produced; a closure that included it would never converge. Narrowing the envelope to the 30 denominator-derived targets removes that dependency rather than papering over it: a workspace test target outside the envelope can change freely, and only ordinary Rust CI — not this campaign — runs and fails on it. Workspace documentation tests are a third, separate obligation the campaign has always run regardless of the accepted scope, because they execute committed rustdoc examples rather than reading anything dynamic; `workspace framework and adapter source` and `spike source` below stay whole-crate for that reason, not because every workspace test target runs.

workspace framework and adapter source.why: Every scenario the accepted scope assigns runs against this code, and the workspace documentation tests exercise the rustdoc examples committed in it.

spike source.why: The M0 architecture and M6 item-hot-path spikes are workspace members `cargo test --workspace --all-features --doc` covers, so a failing rustdoc example there fails the campaign's documentation-test obligation even though the campaign does not run either spike's own test targets.

migrations.why: The durable schema the accepted scope's PostgreSQL-backed scenarios migrate to before they run.

campaign implementation.why: The exact test targets the accepted-scope document's 133 assignments name — the execution envelope — plus the shared support modules those targets compile against. A workspace test file not listed here is outside the envelope: it is not selected, so it is neither run by the campaign nor able to affect its result, including every other M5 campaign's own reconciliation test. A test inside a listed target that is not itself an assigned scenario is a different case: it still runs, because selected targets run in full, and its own source is covered by the same target file being listed.

cargo manifests.why: Feature selection, dependency ranges, and which targets `cargo metadata` reports at all. A campaign built with different features, or resolving its required targets against a different metadata graph, is a different campaign. Every workspace member's manifest is listed, including the spikes and xtask: `cargo metadata` resolves the whole workspace at once, so a malformed manifest anywhere prevents the producer from resolving its target set.

dependency resolution.why: The exact dependency graph the whole workspace suite was built from.

toolchain and build configuration.why: The compiler the whole workspace is built with, and the cargo configuration it is built under.

campaign fixtures.why: The declared denominator — the accepted M0-M4 ledger disposition, the 42-row scope, and the 133 scenario assignments — and this closure itself. The producer derives its required-target set from this document, so a change to it can change which test targets the campaign runs as well as which scenarios it requires from them.

conformance execution contract.why: How CI actually runs the campaign: the supported matrix, the database it is given, the command, and the environment. The dedicated workflow is included with them, and its contract-check step fails closed if the workflow drifts from the contract. An unrelated CI job in ci.yml does not invalidate retained conformance evidence, while any change to the dedicated conformance workflow does.

independent verifier.why: The program that decides whether a report proved what it owed and whether retained evidence is still what it says. Its verdicts are part of the campaign result, so a report produced under a different verifier is a result under a different standard. Listed as the specific files that implement it, matching the soak, cancellation, and performance campaigns' own closures, rather than the whole `xtask/src` directory: `main.rs` dispatches the command, `conformance.rs` derives the required-target set and reconciles the suite against it, `evidence.rs` is the permanent offline verifier, and `suite.rs` is the target-running and libtest-parsing mechanics every M5 runner shares.
